data.description:
## Description

**What**: Create plugins/dso/docs/contracts/review-findings-schema.md (relation enum, prior_finding_id rules, escape_rationale format, NEW_INTRODUCED-vs-NEW_PRE_EXISTING semantics). Create plugins/dso/docs/contracts/review-defenses.md (DefenseStore record shape: prior_finding_id, cited_lines_fingerprint, defense_text up to 4096 chars, defender, cycle_number, timestamp, severity_history[], optional arbiter_ruling).
**Why**: Foundation for SC1, SC3, SC4. All downstream stories reference these contracts. Doing this first prevents drift between stories.
**Scope**:
  IN:
  - review-findings-schema.md created and reviewed
  - review-defenses.md created and reviewed
  - Both contracts referenced from reviewer-base.md and review-fix-dispatch.md
  OUT:
  - Implementation code (covered by S6, S7, S8)

## Done Definitions

- When this story is complete, the relation taxonomy and DefenseStore record shape are documented as canonical contracts that all reviewer agents and orchestrator code reference
  ← Satisfies: "Stateful re-review with two-call reviewer architecture, orchestrator-side proximity-overlap verification, and severity-history telemetry"
- Unit tests written and passing for all new or modified logic

## Considerations

- [Maintainability] Contract docs use the same structural pattern as existing plugins/dso/docs/contracts/ files

## Escalation Policy

**Escalation policy**: Proceed unless a significant assumption is required to continue — one that could send the implementation in the wrong direction. Escalate only when genuinely blocked without a reasonable inference. Document all assumptions made without escalating.
data.title: As a developer, I have review-findings-schema.md and review-defenses.md contract documents defining the relation taxonomy and DefenseStore record shape
